correctness.rationale: Exact matrix norm identity for a planar normal oscillator reduces the objective to product of positive q. An exact strictly convex pair-product polynomial excludes any unequal positive steps. The log curvature gives global Jensen optimality when b<=a. For b>a, U(t)=t g'(t)-g(t) has exactly one positive root; f=g/t is strictly unimodal; the adjacent-step comparison has exactly one positive crossing, proving every phase and tie case. Three critical identities were symbolically checked in check.py; 37,500 random schedules supplement but do not prove globality.

value.rationale: The natural fixed-duration, finite-solve-budget numerical-damping question is completely classified, rather than optimized only over one arbitrary parameter slice. A structural pair-replacement theorem forces equal active steps; exact adjacent active-count thresholds and a sharp b=a bifurcation give an efficient global prescription for any N. The rational four-step example reduces squared numerical amplification by 19.64% against equal use of all four steps. This is damping, not a demonstrated accuracy or runtime improvement.
